methodology: Per-ayah first-pass textual screening. Quran Arabic and English checked at legacy.quran.com/11/26-44; Genesis Hebrew and English consulted at sefaria.org/Genesis.6-9. ayat.assessment: Noah's exclusive worship warning and threatened painful punishment; Genesis 6:5–7 gives divine judgment of wickedness, not Noah's monotheistic speech.
Elite reject Noah as merely human and disparage socially low-status followers; Genesis 6–9 does not narrate this exchange.
Noah argues from clear evidence and mercy without coercing unwilling hearers; no verse-specific equivalent established in Genesis 6–9.
Noah refuses payment and expulsion of believers; Genesis flood narrative has no equivalent dialogue; later traditions need source-specific inspection.
Noah asks who could protect him if he drove away believers; no precise equivalent established in examined Genesis passages.

staged_candidates.relationship: shared judgment setting / significant narrative contrast
staged_candidates.similarity: Divine punishment against a wicked generation before the Flood
staged_candidates.difference: Genesis has God's judgment and decision; Qur'an gives Noah's direct monotheistic warning to his people.
